summary.headline: MOFSL FY26 operating PAT rose 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores; Q4 operating PAT up 25% with a ₹661 crore exit run rate.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 operating PAT of ₹2,360 crores (+16% YoY), with Q4 operating PAT up 25% and the strongest of the four quarters. Asset and Private Wealth businesses grew profit 33% and now contribute about 50% of operating PAT, with Asset Management at 33% of group operating PAT versus 26% in FY25. Reported PAT including OCI was hit by notional MTM losses of about ₹1,000 crores on a ~₹9,000 crore investment book, which management said were largely recouped in April 2026. Long-term credit rating was upgraded to AA+ (stable). Q&A focused on SIP and MF flow share, yield compression from product mix, MTF and broking trajectory, digital broker competition, and treasury MTM.

Asset Management share of group operating PAT

financial_highlights.value: ~₹9,000 crores (~₹1,000 crores at consolidated level per analyst)
Up ~10% YoY; marketing & tech ~5.5% of net revenues

segments.name: Asset Management (AMC + Alternates)
segments.commentary: AMC AUM crossed ₹1.5 lakh crores; FY26 net flows ₹70,000 crores across AMC and PWM; SIP flows ₹16,000+ crores (+78% YoY), 4.7% market share, SIP AUM ~₹30,000 crores. Alternates fee-earning AUM grew 40% to ₹21,000 crores after IBEF V (~$1 billion).

segments.name: Private Wealth Management
segments.commentary: ARR AUM ₹46,000 crores; 440+ RMs with 32% having 3+ years vintage; AUM per RM rose from ~₹300 crores to ₹450 crores; ~9,000 families served, about half with UHNI potential.

segments.name: Wealth Management (broking & distribution)
segments.commentary: Broking now 35% of wealth revenue vs 60% five years ago; retail equity ADTO share 8.6% in FY26, up ~100bps for the year; Q4 brokerage revenue up ~33% YoY.

segments.name: Capital Markets (Investment Banking / ECM)
segments.commentary: 52 deals in FY26 raising ₹83,600 crores; ranked #2 in capital markets league table and #1 in QIP league table; coverage at 360 companies with aim of ~500.

segments.name: Housing Finance (MOHFL)
segments.commentary: Adjusted disbursements +28% to ₹2,291 crores and AUM +25% to ₹6,100 crores; raised $100 million from ADB; management expects strong growth over 2-3 years without external equity.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Asset and Private Wealth profit share to keep rising in FY27 as they grow faster than the rest of the group.
AMC: SIP run rate ~₹1,400-1,500 crores per month (~₹18,000 crores annualised); AUM already ₹1.8 lakh crores, 15% above FY26 average; 8 funds to cross 3-year vintage by Mar'27 and 16 by Mar'28.
Management expects brokerage revenue to catch up in coming periods as regulatory impact on F&O is behind and volumes have recovered; no numeric FY27 broking guidance given.
MTF: management expects strong growth similar to the ~40% growth in FY26, though the book fell from ~₹6,500 crores (9M FY26) to ₹5,700 crores at Mar'26 on market impact.
No quantitative guidance on variable additional returns (carry); management expects meaningful accruals in coming periods as several funds are above hurdles.
capex_capacity: Private Wealth: calibrated investment in senior leadership and RMs to continue in FY27.
Asset Management: investment team expanded to over 50 members including passives; MF leadership decision pending internal/external evaluation.
Product pipeline: maiden Private Credit fund (₹3,000 crores), first Commercial RE Fund, and Series VII of Residential RE Fund; contra fund launch underway; 17+ active MF products.
GIFT City route being used for inbound and outbound flows.
demand_pricing: MF net flows: Jan'26 weak for active funds, passives strong; Q4 net flows over ₹2,500 crores; April 2026 MF net flow share above AUM share. Redemption pressure peaked Jan-Feb'26, normalised by Mar'26 and below normal in April.
MF flow market share reportedly fell from ~7.5% to ~3% (analyst figure); SIP share dipped in Q4 due to international funds closed to new money and a microcap fund locked.

TER changes did not impact fees; fees for the unaffected cohort improved slightly. Alternates retention rates maintained; yield compression attributed to mix (faster-growing passives have lower retention).

Digital brokers are gaining share in cash and F&O and as MF distributors (analyst cited 60-70% of new SIPs via fintech platforms); management says wealth model is research and advisory led and focusing on high-value traders.
Wealth transaction income in Q4 boosted by insurance distribution revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP market share dip in the quarter and what is being done to regain it?
qa_highlights.answer: SIP run rate is ₹1,400+ crores per month; passive decline due to international funds closed to new money and a locked microcap fund, with a small active drop. SIP books are at last-year levels and should climb as performance recovers.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving revenue yield compression and the lending growth in Private Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: TER changes had no fee impact. Compression is mix-driven, as passives (lower retention) grew fastest. Private Wealth lending is a strategy to offer solutions to UHNIs and family offices, combining loans against securities and investment assets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF book guidance for FY27 and the QoQ decline?
qa_highlights.answer: The decline (₹6,500 crores at 9M to ₹5,700 crores at Mar'26) is market-driven and industry-wide. Management is confident of strong growth, citing ~7% cash and MTF share and a strong balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹1,000 crore treasury loss unrealised and has it been recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it is a notional MTM loss under Ind AS, with most recouped in April 2026. The investment book's 10-year-plus IRR is ~18%, and including buybacks and dividends it has compounded at ~40% p.a.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned against digital brokers and fintech SIP platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth model is research and advisory led across franchisee, direct and branch channels; cash market revenue share held. Wealth distribution AUM grew 40% to ~₹44,000 crores. Working on high-value trader positioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Private Wealth client quality and AUM per RM trend?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM per RM rose from ~₹300 crores a couple of years ago to ₹450 crores at Mar'26 despite a larger RM base. Among ~9,000 families, almost 50% have UHNI potential. Segments are HNI (₹50-100 crores), UHNI (₹100 crores+) and family offices.

risks_watch: Unrealised MTM on the ~₹9,000 crore investment book; quarterly volatility in reported PAT (management says most was recouped in April 2026).
Market share pressure from digital and discount brokers in cash, F&O and SIP flows; MF net flow share needs to stay above AUM share.
Yield compression from passive-heavy mix and TER changes; Alternates yield dependent on variable returns timing.
Q4 other expenses up ~20% QoQ on marketing, brand and CSR; FY27 run rate of these costs unclear.
MTF book fell QoQ; growth recovery depends on market conditions.
Leadership vacancy on the MF investment side pending decision.
summary.management_tone: Confident on structural growth in AMC, Alternates and Private Wealth, and on the rebound in Q4 volumes and flows. Cautious and evasive on specifics: no numeric guidance on broking, MTF, or carry, and deflected the treasury MTM question to notional accounting.
key_quotes: Our operating profit after tax in the year FY26 grew by 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores, led by a 33% growth in the profits of Asset and Private Wealth businesses.
We exit the last quarter with an operating PAT run rate of ₹661 crores.
It is a notional mark -to-market loss. We revalue all our Long-only investments at mark -to-market based on the Ind AS requirements & that's why these are notional losses .
Whilst our size has increased over time, our ambitions have never been boutique .

adds.what: Maiden Private Credit fund (₹3,000 crores), first Commercial RE Fund, Series VII of Residential RE Fund (fund launches, not productive capacity)

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management expects Asset and Private Wealth profit share to keep rising and brokerage to catch up, backed by AUM already at ₹1.8 lakh crores (15% above FY26 average), SIP run-rate of ~₹1,400-1,500 crores/month and new fund launches, though no capacity additions or firm order book are quantified.
